subject: math

objective.text: Draw a line plot to show measurement data. Relate the measurement scale to the number line.

explanations.title: What a line plot is
explanations.text: A line plot shows data on a number line. Put an X above the number for each measurement. Write the unit. Give the plot a title, like a bar graph.

explanations.title: From tally marks to X's
explanations.text: Each tally mark in the table becomes one X. Every X is the same size. Stack the X's above the number.

explanations.title: Data may not start at zero
explanations.text: Sometimes the data start at a number like 3. Two slashes show that some numbers are skipped. The first label is the shortest measurement. The last label is the longest.

explanations.title: Label every number
explanations.text: Label every number from the shortest to the longest. Do this even when no item has that measure. The steps on a number line must be equal. An empty spot shows a gap in the data.

explanations.title: A ruler is a number line
explanations.text: One box on centimeter grid paper is 1 centimeter. The centimeters on a ruler are like the numbers on a number line. Your line plot can match the ruler.

examples.title: Shoe lengths
examples.text: The shortest shoe is 19 centimeters. The longest is 26 centimeters. No shoe is 23 or 24 centimeters. Still label 19 to 26 on the number line.

examples.title: Handspans
examples.text: The handspan number line goes from 3 to 8 inches. It has two slashes after zero. Each tally mark becomes an X above its number of inches.

questions.text: Mike, Dennis and April have 24 pennies, 15 nickels, 7 dimes and 2 quarters. The pennies are in one cup. The other coins are in a second cup. How many coins are in the second cup?
The pennies cup has 24 coins. Which cup has more coins, and how many more?
On a line plot, where do we put an X for each measurement?
A handspan number line has two slashes between zero and 3. What do the two slashes show?
Every line plot needs a name at the top. What do we call that name?

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 1 (we always give a line plot a title)

questions.text: How wide is one box on centimeter grid paper?
How is a ruler like a number line?
How do you know the first and last numbers to label on a line plot?
Shoes are from 19 centimeters to 26 centimeters long. How many numbers do you label, counting both 19 and 26?
No shoe was 23 centimeters or 24 centimeters long. Do we label those numbers on the line plot?
A table has 4 tally marks at 6 inches and 2 tally marks at 7 inches. How many X's are on the line plot in all?
What other graphs do line plots remind you of?
Our handspan number line did not start at 0 or 1. Why?
Could we label only 19, 20, 21, 22 and 26 on the shoe number line? Why or why not?
Why do we put marks at 23, 24 and 25 centimeters when no shoe has those lengths?
Tell one good thing and one hard thing about a tally chart and a line plot.

Count every whole number from the shortest to the longest. Do not skip any.

Add up the coins in each cup. Then compare the two totals.
